main_text.p: Regionum interualla, & urbium insignium loca, Præterea cœli & stellarum figuras uidisse pictas in tabulis, quas ueteres Aegyptij circumuecti ultimas terræ metas artificiosè pingi & in templis & firmissimis arcibus collocari curauerint.

Etsi autem ut in poëmate, narratio fabulosa est: tamen hæc uerissima sunt, Antiquitatem studiosè hanc doctrinam de terræ magnitudine & metis, de regionum interuallis, de motibus cœlestibus inquisiuisse, ilustrasse & propagasse, & quidem studia præcipua huius sapientiæ fuisse non solum in Aegypto, sed etiam in Chaldæa & Phœnicum urbibus, ubi semina sparserant & ante diluuium sapientissimi uiri, & postea filij Nohæ.
Nec uero dubium est, illos summos uiros cum docerent suam posteritatem de Deo, de discrimine generis

page.notes: The last word "neris" stands alone at the right and is the end of "generis" continued; transcribed as printed from the scan. Some letters are blurred in the scan (for example "ilustrasse", "fur-isse"), and the reading "illustrasse" is uncertain; "sed eti-am" is printed with a line break. The text reads "ilustrasse", "propagasse" and "fuisse" as printed; "ilustrasse" may be an error for "illustrasse" in print.
